bull.b: Alphabet’s scale drives very high and improving margins across its core businesses. Sustained gross and net margin strength reflects dominant pricing power in advertising plus operating leverage in Cloud and AI, supporting durable earnings power even as growth moderates.

A low leverage profile and a large cash and marketable securities base give Alphabet flexibility to fund heavy AI capex, strategic M&A, and shareholder returns. The conservative capital structure increases resilience to macro shocks and supports long-term investment plans.

Rapid Cloud revenue growth and a sizable, contract-backed backlog signal durable structural demand as enterprises adopt AI and cloud services. Large multi-year contracts and accelerating enterprise adoption improve revenue visibility and should support sustained, high-margin Cloud contribution.

bear.t: Very large CapEx pressure on free cash flow
bear.b: Alphabet’s aggressive AI infrastructure build raises durable capital intensity and depresses free cash flow conversion. Persistently elevated CapEx reduces near-term distributable cash and constrains margin expansion until new capacity and monetization ramp in subsequent years.

bear.t: Significant recent capital raises and complex securities
bear.b: Material equity offerings, mandatory convertible preferreds and multi‑tenor debt increase balance sheet complexity and create potential dilution or restrictions (preferred dividends/conversion mechanics). These actions limit flexibility for buybacks/dividends and alter long‑term capital structure dynamics.

bear.t: Supply constraints and margin headwinds for Cloud
bear.b: Capacity bottlenecks that force reliance on third‑party providers raise unit costs and compress Cloud margins until internal TPU/system delivery scales. Delayed TPU revenue recognition and bridging arrangements create execution risk and margin uncertainty across the multi‑quarter AI infrastructure build.
